question: After ungraceful process exit at immutable file publication boundaries, does reopening distinguish pending, corrupted, completed and body-verified evidence without helper replay?

body.reason: Frozen owned synthetic subprocess fault body for publication-boundary research; no real retrieval or quote.

method: Child process calls existing owned JobBudget and descriptor write_new using own new directories. Mid-write interception performs half an os.write then os._exit(91); no cleanup/finally. Other boundaries exit after existing call returns. Reopen in separate parent; no helper requests/parser/network/model calls. Missing/tampered body forks copy completed journals and never delete/modify original completed case.
limits: Actual process interruption only, not host crash/powerloss/Metal/nativeadapterrestore. Unfsynced partial bytes may be visible through OS cache; no disk durability inferred.
REFUSED from partial journal is safe integrity behavior, not completed recovery. UNKNOWN_COMPLETION forbids replay.
After_config reopen reserve is an explicit owned control call that creates its first reservation, not startup auto dispatch; no helper dispatched.
Budget completion metadata hashes do not prove payload availability/integrity; separate body gate checks existence/exacthash.
No production or permanent test modifications; results do not apply an atomic-publication fix.
